title: Generic quasi-separatedness of a finite type morphism
statement: Let $h:Z\to T$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with $T$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. There is a nonempty open subscheme $W\subseteq T$ such that $h^{-1}(W)\to W$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Neither $T$ nor $Z$ is assumed Noetherian, and $h$ is not assumed separated or quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 052A, proposition-generic-flatness, quasi-separatedness conclusion in the last paragraph of its proof

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$. By [def-pc-integral-scheme], $A$ is a domain. The finite-affine-cover characterization of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives a finite cover $h^{-1}(V)=\bigcup_{i=1}^n Z_i$, where $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and each $B_i$ is a finite type $A$-algebra. By the Zariski topology on [def-weil-affine-spectrum], closed subsets are zero loci of ideals. For each ordered pair choose an ideal $I_{ij}\subseteq B_i$ defining the closed subset $Z_i\setminus(Z_i\cap Z_j)$, and put $M_{ij}=B_i/I_{ij}$. This is a finite $B_i$-module, generated by the class of $1$; no finite generation of $I_{ij}$ is asserted. If the source over $V$ is empty, the cover and the pairs are empty.

Apply [lem-pur-generic-finite-module-presentation] to each $(A,B_i,M_{ij})$. Its hypotheses hold because $A$ is a domain, $B_i$ is finite type, and $M_{ij}$ is cyclic. Obtain nonzero $a_{ij}\in A$ such that $(M_{ij})_{a_{ij}}$ is finitely presented over $(B_i)_{a_{ij}}$. Put $a=\prod_{i,j}a_{ij}$ (the empty product is $1$). This is nonzero in a domain, so $W=D(a)\subseteq V\subseteq T$ contains the prime ideal $(0)$ of $A$ and is nonempty. Each $a_{ij}$ is invertible after inverting $a$: its inverse is $(\prod_{(k,l)\ne(i,j)}a_{kl})/a$. Localize the finite presentation matrices at these further elements to obtain finite presentations of $(M_{ij})_a$ over $(B_i)_a$. Explicitly localization preserves exactness: if a fraction maps to zero, multiplying its numerator by a denominator makes it lie in the original kernel, so the original image representation supplies a localized preimage. Thus this common shrinking retains all the module finite presentations.

A prime of $B_i$ lies over $D(a)$ exactly when it does not contain the image of $a$. Thus the inverse image of $W$ in $Z_i$ is $D(a)$ in that chart; [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] identifies this open subscheme with the affine $Z_{i,a}=\operatorname{Spec}(B_i)_a$. Its intersection with $Z_{j,a}$ is the complement of $V(I_{ij}(B_i)_a)$. The quotient module $(M_{ij})_a$ is $(B_i)_a/I_{ij}(B_i)_a$: send $(b+I_{ij})/a^r$ to $b/a^r$ modulo the extended ideal; the fraction equality criterion makes this a well-defined bijection. Its support is exactly that zero locus. Indeed, if $\mathfrak p$ does not contain the ideal, an ideal element outside $\mathfrak p$ becomes a unit and kills the quotient; if the ideal is contained in $\mathfrak p$, the localized quotient maps onto the residue field at $\mathfrak p$ and is nonzero. Apply [lem-pur-finitely-presented-support-complement] to the presentations from step 2. It follows that every $Z_{i,a}\cap Z_{j,a}$ is quasi-compact.

The $Z_{i,a}$ form a finite affine open cover of $h^{-1}(W)$ with quasi-compact pairwise intersections. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion] therefore makes this source scheme quasi-separated, including the empty source case. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] says that a morphism whose source is quasi-separated is quasi-separated, with no condition on its target. Apply it to $h^{-1}(W)\to W$. This proves the required conclusion, without having assumed quasi-separatedness of the original map or Noetherianity.
